item.title: Mariners raised an American flag after clinching their division days after 9/11; 25 years later...
item.description: In a celebration of unity and triumph, a new bronze statue honors a pivotal moment in Seattle Mariners history. It features two former players hoisting the American flag, capturing the spirit of their victorious 2001 division title. This monument is situated in a modern plaza that includes interactive components and fundraising initiatives, with proceeds dedicated to restoring youth baseball and softball fields across Washington state.

item.title: Meet Kiran Reddy, 18-year-old Georgia teen who became the first Indian American to win Miss Teen USA
item.description: Kiran Reddy has made an outstanding mark as the first Indian American crowned Miss Teen USA. Having previously claimed the Miss Georgia Teen USA title, she is celebrated as Georgia's first national winner. A dedicated pre-medical student, Reddy aspires to inspire young girls. She is set to represent the United States at the Miss Teen Universe contest, alongside continuing her academic journey.

item.title: Baltimore shopping centre rebounds as 200 community investors take ownership, with 10 new leases and 100+ jobs
item.description: Edmondson Village Shopping Center is undergoing a significant transformation driven by local residents. Two hundred community investors now hold a direct ownership stake in the property. Ten new leases have been signed, bringing essential services to the neighborhood. A planned headquarters for Meals on Wheels will create over one hundred jobs. This community ownership model connects residents to the property's economic revival.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Oakland woman lost $12,145 after scammers posed as Charles Schwab security
item.description: An Oakland woman says scammers posing as Charles Schwab security drained her entire $12,145 investment account after a frantic phone call. She denies sharing any information, while Schwab said its investigation found that a verification code was provided to a third party. She is now taking the case to arbitration and has contacted police and the FBI.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How a stranger's advice helped Tiffany Haddish go from living in her car to bying 17 properties
item.description: Tiffany Haddish went from experiencing homelessness and living on a $500-a-month budget to building a real estate portfolio of about 17 properties. She credits advice from an accountant she met during a trip to China and Japan for changing her approach to money. She also used acting pay cheques to buy and pay off property.

item.title: Former Ravens coach John Harbaugh's 1905 Maryland stone mansion sells for $6M
item.description: Former Baltimore Ravens coach John Harbaugh has sold his historic stone mansion in Owings Mills, Maryland, for $6 million. He bought the 9-acre property for $3 million in 2013. Built in 1905, the 9,100-square-foot home has five bedrooms, a carriage house, four-car garage, pool, hot tub and multiple outdoor spaces.

item.title: Crossing Guard Shields Family: Las Vegas worker steps between car and children; dashcam video goes viral
item.description: In a heart-stopping moment, a crossing guard in Las Vegas, Richard Jones, heroically leapt into action to save a mother and her children from an oncoming vehicle near Pinecrest Academy St. Rose. The shocking dashcam footage revealed how close they came to disaster. Grateful for his bravery, the family later returned to express their heartfelt thanks, emphasizing the inherent dangers faced by crossing guards in school zones.

item.title: Three women survived a deadly Grand Canyon flood after clinging to a rock ledge for 5 hours
item.description: Three women survived a dangerous flash flood in the Grand Canyon. They clung to a rock ledge for five hours while debris swept past. Separated briefly, each feared the others had been lost to the waters. A rescue helicopter eventually spotted the stranded hikers and brought them to safety. This survival occurred during a larger disaster which claimed other lives.

item.title: A giant 10-sided wave is emerging around Saturn’s south pole, Hubble observations show
item.description: Saturn's south pole reveals a giant, evolving 10-sided atmospheric wave. Hubble telescope observations trace subtle signs of this pattern back to 2023. This newly identified feature is embedded in a powerful jet stream and extends through multiple atmospheric layers. Scientists have searched for a southern counterpart to the northern hexagon for decades. This discovery offers a rare chance to observe a major atmospheric pattern developing in real time.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: A $5.5M Portland power project could remove 400 trees from Forest Park while powering over 55,000 homes; the deal has split conservation groups
item.description: Amidst rising concerns, Portland General Electric's tree-removal project has drawn fervent opposition from conservationists who fear for the health of mature forests and wildlife. While the utility argues that this initiative is crucial for ensuring consistent power to households, the city is in the process of evaluating a new application and awaiting feedback from the staff. The decision will ultimately balance environmental impacts with the necessity of electrical reliability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tech entrepreneur's Martha's Vineyard estate bought for $19 million sells for record $43 million
item.description: A 31.59-acre estate in Edgartown on Martha’s Vineyard has sold for a record $43 million. Tech entrepreneur Michael Bronner spent $19.125 million between 2019 and 2023 assembling the property, which includes an 8,994-square-foot, 12-bedroom home. The sale surpassed both the island’s previous $37.5 million record and Massachusetts’ $38.1 million record.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: The story of Tsutomu Yamaguchi, the only survivor of both Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings
item.description: Tsutomu Yamaguchi's remarkable story is one of survival against unimaginable odds, as he endured the horrors of two atomic bombings just days apart in August 1945. Initially in Hiroshima on August 6, he found himself in Nagasaki on August 9. Post-war, Yamaguchi channeled his experiences into activism, passionately advocating for nuclear disarmament at the United Nations, illustrating the catastrophic effects of nuclear armament.
